newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wary German shares start unchanged before US data.
newsitem.headline: Wary German shares start unchanged before US data.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade largely unchanged on Thursday and were not expected to make any major movements before U.S. producer price and jobless claims data due later in the day.
The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares traded half a point lower at 2,566.30 on small turnover, with September DAX futures flat at 2,569.5 shortly before their expiry next week.
"It looks as if we're going nowhere at the moment until the U.S. numbers," said one. The dollar, trading firm at 1.5084/91 to the mark, was meanwhile seen offering some support.
The U.S. data will be above all examined for clues on the timing and extent of future U.S. interest rate moves.
U.S. producer prices are expected to rise between 0.1 and 0.2 percent in August, with U.S. jobless claims in the latest 7-month period expected to gain between 315-360,000.
Any indications of inflationary pressures in the U.S. could hit German shares hard, dealer said.

Individual share movements were limited. Commercial bank Deutsche Bank gained 35 pfennigs to 71.60 marks after news of an upgrade from "hold" to "buy" from investment bank UBS provided relief from recent problems with its British asset management unit.

Car-maker BMW lost 8.00 marks to 860 after a company forecast that full-year earnings growth would be around the 10 percent level of the first half was seen as disappointing some of the more bullish expectations.
